what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat heart failure. It helps your heart pump blood more effectively, reduces the chances of going to the hospital because of heart failure, and helps you live longer. It works by relaxing your blood vessels and reducing the workload on your heart.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same times every day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time, usually every 2 to 4 weeks, until you reach the right dose for you. The usual starting dose is 24/26 mg twice a day (two times a day). The target dose for most people is 97/103 mg twice a day. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than 6 hours away. If your next dose is less than 6 hours away, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not take ACE inhibitors (such as lisinopril, enalapril, or ramipril) while taking this medicine. You must wait at least 36 hours after stopping an ACE inhibitor before starting sacubitril/valsartan, and vice versa. Do not take aliskiren (Tekturna) if you have diabetes. Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes that contain potassium unless your doctor approves them, as they can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid drinking alcohol excessively, as it can lower your blood pressure too much. Be careful when standing up quickly, as this medicine can cause dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: sudden swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this could be a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); severe dizziness or fainting; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness or tingling; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination; or if you become pregnant. Also call your doctor if you feel your heart failure symptoms are getting worse, such as increased shortness of breath, swelling in your legs or ankles, or sudden weight gain.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away in your body, but you may not feel the benefits for several weeks. Most people notice improvements in their symptoms, such as less shortness of breath and more energy, within a few weeks to months. It is very important to keep taking this medicine every day even if you feel well, because it is protecting your heart over time.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine. If you become pregnant, stop taking it immediately and call your doctor. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure, so your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver issues. Always tell your doctor about all your health conditions before starting this medicine.
